item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Mona Labib — Wed Sep 2, 12:00 AM — Agincourt
item.description:
Throughout the month of September, works by artist Mona Labib are on display at Agincourt Branch. Mona Labib is a professional IT Project Manager who loves the arts. Most of her works are in oil. Throughout her career, arts and painting provided an escape from the daily stresses of her job and a means of relaxation. Although she has been painting and taking art lessons for many years, she still considers herself very much a beginner. This exhibit is part of TPL's Art Exhibits Space program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods. The exhibit can be viewed during Agincourt branch open hours. Please check the Agincourt branch page before your visit. Free. All are welcome. Image credit: Mona Labib; oil; "Sunset at the Beach"
Source: Toronto Public Library — Adults

item.title: Improv Class for New Friends — Sat Sep 12, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Improv For New Friends Don't be disappointed if you don't see a bunch of people attending. I advertise this on multiple platforms and the class usually sells out.
\*\*If you don't use Paypal, email me at ralph@socap.ca and we'll figure it out. You can pay be etransfer or with a credit card/cash at the venue.\*\*
Improv comedy uses several techniques to create laughter. These include, creating an atmosphere free of judgement, saying 'yes', active listening, being positive, putting your focus on others, and the importance of play and laughter.
Not coincidentally, these are the same things that happen to us naturally when we are bonding with another person.
In this class, we'll explore these techniques not with the goal of being funny, but with the goal of being people that other people want to be around.

item.title: NatureTO: Trees Around the Branch Tour — Wed Sep 16, 5:00 PM — Flemingdon Park
item.description:
The Flemingdon Park branch and its neighbourhood is home to a variety of trees. Join the City of Toronto Urban Forestry team to explore the natural world on a local neighbourhood tour. Learn how to recognize different species and fun facts about their cultural and ecological importance. Children under 12 must be accompanied by a parent/caregiver. Registration is required.
